instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Not About Who Lost
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on rules, effort, or next steps instead of the result that embarrasses you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the quiz score away. I taught you to revise the questions you missed; let's start with geography.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did we come last?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're asking about the whole team now. Good. Which capital did we spend ten minutes arguing over?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many points did we actually get?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the total folded over. Point to the geography questions, the way I used to mark your practice sheets. Tell me which country we're revising first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's review your pacing, not my finish time. Remember the breathing rhythm I taught you on this track?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You stopped halfway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you noticed where; better than staring at your shoes. Tell me how you were breathing when you passed me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everybody else finished. You're the only one who stopped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll discuss my time after your breathing. Take four steps for me now, in for two and out for two. You used to rush the out-breath.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first checkmate against me. Take a photograph; that's the corner trap I showed you last week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why didn't you use your queen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was working with the other pieces. You actually watched my king this time, instead of chasing everything shiny.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you go easy on me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You found the trap without me pointing. Take your photograph and tell me which move you're proud of.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First prize, Mum. Those folding lessons paid off; you've stopped beating every bit of air out of the batter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your cake isn't on the judging table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine's staying in the kitchen for tea. Yours finally rose above the tin. Tell me what you did differently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You withdrew so I'd win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Seven other cakes were still there. Cut yours and show me the crumb, the way I taught you. Let's see what beat them.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Admit What You Wanted
cards.instruction: Maneuver them into revealing which outcome they truly wanted before you explain your own stake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I tell you who won the chair's election, Jo or Nina—which did you want? Give your own answer, the way I taught you in debate practice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You look disappointed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An observation before a guess; you're improving. Now leave my face out of it. Jo or Nina?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tell me your choice first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write yours down and slide it to me before I answer. You used to change every argument when you saw my notes; let me see one name you chose without them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which job did you want me to take—the local one or the one abroad? We practised giving a straight answer when I coached your interviews.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever makes you happy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very considerate; you used to answer only for yourself. Now I need that old answer. Did you want me nearby?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does it matter now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because I haven't told you my decision. Finish the sentence we practised: 'I wanted you to take...' Give me the place before I give you mine.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Investment in the Next Round
cards.instruction: Describe defeat, penalty, or a bad bargain as a deliberate investment in a larger future win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That failed market-stall contest bought us the judges' full report. An investment. I taught you to read what a customer wants, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We entered to win the prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're watching revenue now; good. We paid to find out which stall they'll fund next year. Start our new bid with what the judges asked for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't afford another entry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we sell the advice to someone who can. Open the costing sheet I taught you to use; put our lost fee in the minimum-price box. We're selling this lesson at a profit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Selling the stall at a loss was our investment in a better business. Get the margin sheet; I taught you to check costs before admiring the bunting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which better business?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mobile cart. No stall rent, and you finally know what that rent did to our takings. Price the cart for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's an expensive lesson.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put zero in the rent column, then work out how many lunches repay the loss. No guessing, like your first accounts; show me when this cart makes us more than the stall did.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: I Know How to Win This
cards.instruction: Perform mastery of the rules, odds, and consequences while improvising every decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll open with this horse in the lake. Watch your old teacher; I taught you to check the whole board before choosing a move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There aren't horses. That's the scoring marker.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You identified it without my help this time. We establish the score first, so put it in the lake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not allowed to move it. We both start at zero.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly; zero gives us equal odds. Leave it there and hand me a playing piece instead. I'll demonstrate the opening once you've pointed out where the lake starts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Watch how I win this raffle. I taught you probability; buy my ticket just before the draw, so it lands on top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just buy a ticket. They all go in the drum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remembered the sample space. A late ticket will still be nearest the hand, so we'll wait.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They spin the drum before picking one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then buy now, before the queue gets long. The spin will carry ours into the centre. You learnt to wait for a good position from me; this is it. One ticket.
